title: Left Quillen adjunctions descend through left Bousfield localization
statement: Use model categories, functorial cofibrant replacements and Quillen adjunctions as in [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], and simplicial model categories and derived mapping spaces as in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a simplicial model category and $\mathcal N$ any model category. Let $S$ be a small set of arrows of $\mathcal M$. A fibrant object $Z$ is $S$-local if every $(A\to B)\in S$ induces an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}^h(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(A,Z)$. Assume a model structure $L_S\mathcal M$ exists with the original cofibrations and with weak equivalences exactly the maps inducing equivalences of derived mapping spaces into every fibrant $S$-local object; the derived mapping spaces in this definition use the original model structure. Let $F:\mathcal M\rightleftarrows\mathcal N:U$ be a Quillen adjunction. If $FQ(s)$ is a weak equivalence for each $s\in S$, where $Q$ is a functorial cofibrant replacement in the original structure, then the same adjoint functors give a Quillen adjunction $F:L_S\mathcal M\rightleftarrows\mathcal N:U$.

source.place: Hirschhorn, Model Categories and Their Localizations, Proposition 3.3.18(1), printed p. 63. Simplicial source so homotopy function complexes use the displayed derived mapping-space formula; neither properness nor combinatoriality is needed once the localization exists, and no simpliciality of the target is assumed.
